items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: And George Sims was playing paratone.

ctx.x: Well, who was in Joel Lazard's band?

Well, a couple of fellas. Buddy Johnson and Lucie played with him a while. After he got, when he was young, he was the youngest one. And Frankie Doosen played with him a while. But that's two tramos they had. And George Sims was playing paratone. And another fella who played bass, he named George Stu, was a very bright fella. He was playing bass, drums. Now, the tuba, I don't know that fella was playing tuba. I don't know that fella was playing tuba. But he had a pretty good band, Joel Lazard's band. They called…

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: They had old man George Sims playing biotone. ... I was doing that. I was playing Clannett.

ctx.x: Just called it that. Just called it that. Because it was that Texas and Pacific railroad, I thought maybe they had a band or something.

No, they meant that band. That was Nomm in them. Nomm, yeah. Nomm. Louis La Rooks? Well, there's Louis La Rooks come after. Nomm. Mineta, that's right. That's right. Yeah. Nomm. Louis La Rooks. Not Nomm. Nomm. Not Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Joey Hooker? One used to cut meat there. Oh, Louis La Rooks. That's Louis La Rooks. No, they're not. Joel Azard.
